problems.where: crates/dla-cli/src/alloc/pick.rs:42-53, 364, 376-380 (claim at pick.rs:46-47 and skills/detect-leak-anywhere/references/evidence-and-report.md:136-137; leak test at crates/dla-cli/src/alloc_cmd.rs:2590)
problems.text: A real leak in file-backed memory can now read non-leak. When os.rss_file is the only column that passed the first trend, pick treats the run as "no column passed": the runtime heap decides alone and os.rss is only reported (pick.rs:376-380). So "os.rss, which always votes" is false, and a file-backed growth below the noise of os.rss is not seen by os.rss anyway. Shown on prepared series whose first trend is the real gate over 8 main points (os.rss_file rises every point, os.rss is noisy and fails the gate, the heap column is flat), old code against new code through an env switch on a scratch copy: Go shape (rss 60 MB, noise 3 MB, file +300 KB per point) Leak -> NonLeak; JVM shape (noise 5 MB, +400 KB) Leak -> NonLeak; Node shape (noise 1.5 MB, +150 KB) Leak -> NonLeak; Python trim shape (noise 400 KB, +100 KB) Inconclusive -> NonLeak. With a quiet os.rss that itself reads growth-continues and retained in the same result but did not pass the first trend: Leak -> NonLeak. With no heap column: Leak -> Inconclusive. Unchanged: a bound finding tied to os.rss_file and --column os.rss_file still read Leak. The fixer's leak test covers only the case where os.rss passed the gate too, where the verdict was leak before as well. Direction: keep the plateau vote of os.rss_file and drop only its purge reading (the purge reading is the artifact; plateau with purge not-run reads non-leak, so python-graph-churn still passes), or let it vote when its plateau reads growth-continues; then correct the comment and the reference text.

problems.where: harness/python/sitecustomize.py:475-482; docs/VERIFY.md:521; fixer report item 3 (os.rss "is not a purge-step artifact")
problems.text: The cause is only half found, and the same artifact still makes a flat Python run inconclusive through os.rss, which votes. The Python trim step reads `before` after its own `import ctypes`. Measured in a bare interpreter: that import adds 2272 kB to VmRSS (anon 1656, file 616), and the trim call adds 620 kB more. In fixture runs the `before` reading of os.rss is above the last series point by 1647 to 1663 KB (python-report-memo-bounded, earlier run and mine) and by 2154 to 2191 KB (python-zstd-options-3145, earlier run); os.rss_file by 303 to 307 KB in every Python run. So os.rss reads "growth 1.7 MB, retained" on a flat series. In my run of python-report-memo-bounded on this tree the series was 22.70 to 22.82 MB after the warm-up, `before` was 24.37 to 24.44 MB, and both unbound alloc-tests (A2, A3) read inconclusive for exactly this: os.rss voting, plateau, purge retained, growth 1.75 and 1.79 MB, drop -545 KB. The fixture passed only through its bound probe test. The report and the VERIFY row say no mechanism other than growth could be named for os.rss; for the Python trim purge it is the mechanism of item 2. Direction: fix it in the harness (take `before` from the checkpoint's own reading, as the Node and Go agents do, and load ctypes and libc before the warm-up ends), add the test, and correct the row.

problems.where: docs/VERIFY.md:521 (last sentence of the Resolution cell)
problems.text: False statement: "`python-graph-churn` and `node-price-board-flat` among them (both had failed the earlier run)". node-price-board-flat passed the earlier run (u8acc/dynamic.log:34 "node-price-board-flat: pass"; failures empty in dynamic.json; it is a decoy-control fixture and needs no rule-out). Only python-graph-churn failed there. The fixer's report repeats it ("This was a failing fixture before").

The comment and the row say the other purge kinds read the runtime's files too and that the purge reading of os.rss_file is retained whenever it is taken. The per-kind statement the brief asked for is missing, and two kinds contradict the wording: the Go purge record (harness/go/zz_dla_harness_test.go.tmpl:195, zz_dla_driver_test.go.tmpl:200) and the Node record (harness/node/dla-preload.js:881) carry no os.rss_file, so its purge is never read there (not-run) and its vote was non-leak on a flat run. What I read: Python trim: in the record, the step moves it (measured). Python gc: in the record, the step maps nothing. JVM trim-native-heap and gc: in the record, movement judged by reading only. C driver, shim and Rust trim: in the record, `before` is the checkpoint's own reading. Go and Node: not in the record.

The basis line says "no column passed the gate in the latest trend of the harness" while os.rss_file passed and is listed in the same result (seen in the command-level scenario). The wording was written for peaks; it is now printed for a column of real memory.

The doc of `NoGrowth` still says the column "did not grow above its warm-up value"; it now also covers a growth up to the minimum rise. The reference line 153 is one overlong line after the insertion.

Readings that change under the purge minimum, all following from the decision as written. A strict leak of 2 KB per point (24 KB since the warm-up) with a retained purge: Inconclusive -> NonLeak, unbound and with --column. An os.rss_anon step of 30 KB kept by the trim: Inconclusive -> NonLeak. Plateau not-run with 30 KB retained: Leak -> Inconclusive. A released reading with growth at or below 32 KiB becomes no-growth, so the result loses N-HEADROOM or N-ALLOC (node-template-cache in my run: node.heap_used growth 1584, drop 992, supports N-WARM and N-HWM only). Unchanged: 34 KB retained (Inconclusive), a count gauge with 14 more entries retained (Inconclusive), a Go heap leak of 100 KB retained (column reads Leak), os.rss_anon 68 KB (Inconclusive). In the two earlier local runs no leak fixture has a reading that this rule changes.

The margin is thin on the fixture the fix is for: go.heap_objects of go-gc-tuned-batch rose 17.3 and 20.2 KB over the default 16 points in the earlier local run, against a minimum of 32 KiB; a longer --extra would cross it. On the runner the main slope was lower (31.2 against 40.3 per unit), so the default window is covered. In that local run the same retained reading was hidden by the gc test (headroom); that is what differed on the runner, and the row does not say it. The rows also carry measured sizes (164520 B, 8592 kB and others); the brief's rule says no byte counts, and rows at HEAD already carry such figures, so I leave the call to you.

`a_file_backed_column_votes_when_nothing_else_can` does fail when only the new fallback block is removed (voting is empty), so it is a real test of that block; the report says it was not seen failing. The fallback also makes a lone passed os.vm_data vote, which no test names; no real series lacks os.rss, so the block is close to unreachable.

My scratch builds (bin renamed to dla-n1chk) left these two unit directories in the shared target, 183 MB together; I removed the linked target/debug/dla-n1chk and its .d file, and nothing else outside my scratch dir. Observation for the final run: target/debug/dla was replaced under me during the check (a 21:22 build became a 21:04 artifact of another size), and a scratch copy of the workspace reuses the unit hashes of the real tree here (my scratch build compiled dla-cli only). A scratch build that keeps the bin name `dla` therefore overwrites the shared binary. Rebuild dla before the full dynamic run.
